## Summary

Two changes behind one measurement: the shared split combine of the FROST SDPA forward (`sm100/split_combine`) walked its split axis one memory round trip at a time, and the d256 decode tile's split model priced that combine as a flat cost -- together they made the batch-1 decode route split 64 ways and pay a 40 us combine behind a 12 us kernel.

- **Kernel (`split_combine.py`, the lean fp32-partial path):** splits past the 4-split head group are now loaded in groups of `G_T = 16` (LSE and partial-O rows of the whole group first, then the group's math) in both the max pass and the accumulate pass. The arithmetic order is unchanged -- a slot past `n_splits` re-reads the last split and is selected out of the sums -- so the output is bitwise what it was at every split count (checked output for output against the previous kernel at splits 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 on four decode cells).
- **Model (`heuristics.py`):** `choose_decode_tile_split_kv` adds `s * _DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_PER_PARTIAL` (0.17 KV tiles per partial, fitted on the grouped-load combine) to the split path's cost. The batch-1 optima measured at kv 4K / 32K / 128K (splits 16 / 32 / 64) and the batch-4 x 128K one (16) fall out; every existing B200 pin holds.

## Measurement (Rubin cc 10.7, 212 SMs @ 2376 MHz lock, one exclusive GPU, Qwen3.5-397B 24/2 geometry = 2 KV heads x 12:1 packing, d 256, page 16; device microseconds of the decode tile + combine per step from the profiler over 5 replays; the TensorRT-LLM column is the decode kernel FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 launches for `trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache` on the same cells)

| cell | TensorRT-LLM decode kernel us | FROST before (route) | FROST after (route) | FROST after, best split | speed-up vs before (+X %) | vs the TensorRT-LLM kernel (+X %) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B 1 x kv 4K | 13.8 | 18.8 (split 16: 8.5 + 10.3) | 14.6 (16: 8.6 + 6.0) | 14.6 (16) | +28.8 % | -5.5 % |
| B 1 x kv 32K | 22.7 | 53.7 (64: 11.7 + 42.0) | 24.1 (32: 15.1 + 9.0) | 24.1 (32) | +122.8 % | -5.8 % |
| B 1 x kv 128K | 42.5 | 68.6 (64: 27.5 + 41.1) | 41.6 (64: 27.3 + 14.3) | 41.6 (64) | +64.9 % | +2.2 % |
| B 4 x kv 128K | 95.8 | 101.5 (16: 90.3 + 11.2) | 96.8 (16: 90.3 + 6.5) | 96.8 (16) | +4.9 % | -1.0 % |

The combine alone, batch 1, splits 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64: before 2.8 / 5.1 / 10.3 / 21.3 / 42.7 us (0.63-0.67 us per partial), after 3.0 / 5.2 / 6.0 / 8.9 / 14.3 us (0.17-0.18 us per partial). Speed-ups are `before / after - 1`; the table is one node class and one GPU; A/B/A over alternating processes of the two trees (5 base + 3 fixed), 3 rounds x 100 shuffled launches each with a control twin, every (cell, split) output bitwise identical between the trees (20 / 20), SW power-cap counter delta 0 on every row. The end-to-end serving DECODE step of the gated attention block (CUDA-graph replay, the route chosen by the model itself on this branch: 16 / 32 / 64 / 16): 75.0 / 107.0 / 126.0 / 149.4 -> 69.7 / 78.9 / 97.4 / 144.6 us (+7.7 / +35.5 / +29.3 / +3.3 %); the remaining gap to the vLLM chain on those cells is the projection GEMM tile, a separate change.

## Regression guard on the SM100 line (GB200, cc 10.0, 152 SMs @ 1830 MHz lock, one exclusive GPU; a guard on one node class, not a performance claim)

The combine kernel and the decode split model are shared by the SM100 and Rubin bodies, so the same FlashInfer-shaped paged decode graphs (S_q 1, bf16, page 16, per-batch lengths, no Stats) were timed on both trees on a GB200: the engine's own leading plan per tree, a CUDA-graph replay under CUDA events with an L2 flush before every launch, 3 rounds x 100 and a control twin per cell, the SM clock sampled at the lock and the power-cap counter read around every cell, alternating processes of the two trees (3 before / 3 after). Speed-ups are `before / after - 1`:

| cell | d256, 24/2 (12:1) | d128, 24/2 (12:1) | d128, 32/8 (4:1) |
|---|---|---|---|
| B 1 x kv 32K | 72.2 -> 35.6 us (+103.0 %; split 64 -> 32) | 37.4 -> 32.5 us (+14.8 %; split 16 -> 16) | 48.9 -> 43.1 us (+13.5 %; split 16 -> 16) |
| B 1 x kv 128K | 110.7 -> 77.6 us (+42.7 %; split 64 -> 64) | 86.5 -> 82.4 us (+5.0 %; split 16 -> 16) | 115.2 -> 109.1 us (+5.6 %; split 16 -> 16) |
| B 32 x kv 32K | 323.3 -> 324.1 us (-0.2 %; split 2 -> 2) | 420.4 -> 420.4 us (+0.0 %; split 2 -> 2) | 645.6 -> 644.6 us (+0.2 %; split 1 -> 1) |

No cell loses beyond the run-to-run noise of its unchanged kernel (the B 32 cells run split 1 or 2, inside the head group the grouped walk never touches; their outputs are bitwise identical between the trees). On this part the per-partial term is not refitted here (it was fitted on the Rubin tile; every existing B200 pin holds): the combine at 64 partials reads ~50 us before and ~16 us after the grouped walk, and the batch-1 kv 32K route moves from 64 to 32 splits.

## Tests

- `test/python/sdpa/frost/test_sdpa_split_combine_many_splits.py` (new, L0, any SM100-line part): the dense pointer entry at splits 4 / 5 / 16 / 17 / 20 / 33 / 64 / 65 on a decode-shaped row count and the module's 2 x 3 x 5 x 160 shape, dead rows and a dead LAST split, against the float64 reference.
- `test/python/sdpa/frost/test_split_kv_heuristic.py::test_decode_tile_batch_one_prices_every_partial_of_the_combine` (new; RED on the previous model: 64 at kv 32K) and the existing decode-tile pins unchanged.
- Run at this head: the two modules of this PR at `-m "L0 or L1"` on an SM 10.0 part (152 SMs): 165 passed; on an SM 10.7 part the serving decode and capture modules of the gated attention block (whose decode form rides this combine) plus the paged-decode placement pins: 374 passed; on a host without a Blackwell-family GPU the heuristics, geometry, placement and decode-tile modules: 1319 passed / 139 skipped (the device cells). The API index is unchanged.

## Summary

Two changes behind one measurement: the shared split combine of the FROST SDPA forward (`sm100/split_combine`) walked its split axis one memory round trip at a time, and the d256 decode tile's split model priced that combine as a flat cost -- together they made the batch-1 decode route split 64 ways and pay a 40 us combine behind a 12 us kernel.

- **Kernel (`split_combine.py`, the lean fp32-partial path):** splits past the 4-split head group are now loaded in groups of `G_T = 16` (LSE and partial-O rows of the whole group first, then the group's math) in both the max pass and the accumulate pass. The arithmetic order is unchanged -- a slot past `n_splits` re-reads the last split and is selected out of the sums -- so the output is bitwise what it was at every split count (checked output for output against the previous kernel at splits 4 / 8 / 16 / 32 / 64 on four decode cells).
- **Model (`heuristics.py`):** `choose_decode_tile_split_kv` adds `s * _DECODE_TILE_COMBINE_PER_PARTIAL` (0.17 KV tiles per partial, fitted on the grouped-load combine) to the split path's cost. The batch-1 optima measured at kv 4K / 32K / 128K (splits 16 / 32 / 64) and the batch-4 x 128K one (16) fall out; every existing B200 pin holds.

The combine kernel and the decode split model are shared by the SM100 and Rubin bodies, so the same FlashInfer-shaped paged decode graphs (S_q 1, bf16, page 16, per-batch lengths, no Stats) were timed on both trees on a GB200: the engine's own leading plan per tree, a CUDA-graph replay under CUDA events with an L2 flush before every launch, 3 rounds x 100 and a control twin per cell, the SM clock sampled at the lock and the power-cap counter read around every cell, alternating processes of the two trees (3 before / 3 after). +

+pytestmark = [pytest.mark.L0, requires_dsl, requires_blackwell]

+def _partials(b, h, sq, d, splits):
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(20261014 + splits)
+    o = torch.randn(splits, b, sq, h, d, generator=generator) * 0.4
+    lse = torch.randn(splits, b, h, sq, generator=generator) * 2.0 + 0.7
+    if sq > 1:
+        lse[:, :, :, 0] = -torch.inf  # every split dead on one row (a multi-row shape); the decode shape keeps its ONLY row live
+    lse[1, :, :, min(1, sq - 1)] = -torch.inf  # a dead split beside live ones
+    lse[splits - 1, :, 0, :] = -torch.inf  # the LAST split dead on one head: the clamped tail slots re-read it
+    dead = torch.isneginf(lse).permute(0, 1, 3, 2).unsqueeze(-1)
+    o.masked_fill_(dead, torch.nan)  # a dead payload must never enter the arithmetic
+    scores = lse.double()
+    maximum = scores.amax(0)
+    safe_maximum = torch.where(torch.isfinite(maximum), maximum, 0)

+    denominator = weights.sum(0)
+    safe_o = o.double().masked_fill(dead, 0)
+    ref_o = (weights.permute(0, 1, 3, 2).unsqueeze(-1) * safe_o).sum(0) / denominator.clamp_min(1).permute(0, 2, 1).unsqueeze(-1)
+    ref_lse = safe_maximum + denominator.log()
